text: First entry on the new app. Maya keeps saying I should write things down before they fall out of my head, so here we go. Today I sat at the back of the all-hands and watched Devin present the Q4 roadmap. Half of it is my work. He said 'we' a lot. I drank too much of the bad office coffee and didn't say anything. Ran on the river path after work. The light on the Charles is starting to do that early fall thing where everything looks like a postcard you don't deserve.

Sunday. Made the apartment smell like onions and oregano for hours. The bolognese turned out better than the one from Maya's mom, which I will obviously never say out loud. Watched two episodes of something forgettable and went to bed early. Quiet day. Needed it.
Rent goes up $275 in January. Landlord left the notice taped to the door like it was nothing. Stood in the hallway reading it twice. I keep doing the math and the math keeps coming out the same.

Started the short story again. The one about the lighthouse keeper. 600 words before work, then deleted 400 of them at lunch. I think the problem is I keep trying to make him wise. Real people aren't wise, they're just tired and have opinions.

Maya came over and we made the bad frozen pizza on purpose, the kind with the cardboard crust, because she said she missed being twenty. We ate it on the fire escape. She has a freckle on her left shoulder I have looked at a thousand times and somehow noticed again tonight.

Asked Devin for fifteen minutes to talk about the promotion timeline. He said 'soon, soon' and then asked if I could take the Henderson account because he's underwater. I said yes. Of course I said yes. Walked home in the rain without a jacket. Felt almost good.
Mom called. Dad's MRI was clean. I didn't realize how tight my shoulders had been until they dropped on the phone.
Lighthouse story is 2,100 words now. Sent the first half to Priya for notes. She'll be honest, which is what I want, and also what I dread.

Maya said the thing. She said it kindly, on the couch, with the lamp on. She said she loves me and she doesn't know if she's in love with me anymore and she has been sitting with it for months. I asked if there was someone else and she said no and I believed her. We sat there until the radiator clanked on. She slept on the couch. I lay in bed listening to her breathing through the wall like a stranger.
She left for her sister's at noon with a duffel. The apartment is loud in a way I didn't know an apartment could be loud.
Three days. Haven't really eaten. Forgot my laptop charger at the office and didn't go back for it. Priya texted about the story. I haven't opened it.

Devin asked if everything was okay because I missed the Henderson stand-up. I said allergies. He nodded like he wanted that to be true. The promotion conversation feels like it's happening to someone else now.

Went to the laundromat on Cambridge Street because I couldn't face the basement one in our building. Hers basement. Our basement. I don't know. The dryers hummed and I watched a kid try to convince his dad to buy him the green Skittles from the vending machine and I cried into my hood for about ninety seconds and then I was fine. Sort of fine.
$4,180 in checking. Rent, electric, the credit card from the trip in August. After January it gets thin.

Ran four miles on the river path for the first time in weeks. Slowest pace of my life. The leaves are doing the thing. The geese are loud. I kept expecting to feel something profound and instead I just felt my knees.

Priya texted again. I finally wrote back. She said the lighthouse story has a good bone in it but the keeper sounds like he's been to therapy and most people haven't. She's right. She's usually right.

Daylight savings. The 4pm dark is going to be a problem. Made coffee at 6, drank it at the window watching a guy across the courtyard water his plants in a robe. Considered him my friend for a minute.

Maya came to get the rest of her things. She brought her sister to help, which I think was kindness. We didn't really talk. She left the blue Le Creuset because she said I use it more. I am holding the lid right now and I cannot make myself put it down.

Tom from accounting invited me to a Sunday board game thing at his place in Somerville. I almost said no out of habit and then I said yes. Five people I barely know, a dog named Mochi, a game with too many little wooden pieces. I lost badly. Laughed twice on accident. Walked to the T after with my hands in my pockets feeling like a person.
Devin gave the Henderson account to Rachel. Said it was because I'd had a 'rough patch.' I think he meant it as a kindness. I'm not sure I have the energy to be insulted.
Rewrote the opening of the lighthouse story. The keeper is now a man who keeps losing his reading glasses and pretending he didn't. Priya is going to like it more. I like it more.

Couldn't sleep. 3am. Stood at the kitchen counter eating cold leftover rice with a fork, thinking about that summer in Maine when Maya and I rented the cabin with the bad roof. The way she laughed when the bat came in. I don't know what to do with a memory like that now. I don't know where it goes.

Thanksgiving at my brother's in Providence. Five adults, two kids, one overcooked turkey. My niece showed me her drawings of horses for forty straight minutes. She kept saying 'this one is sad because his friend moved' and I had to keep my face very still. Drove back Sunday in the rain. Felt full of something good and something heavy at the same time.
Updated my resume. Just looking. Just looking.

December. Hung the cheap string lights from CVS along the kitchen window. They make the whole place look better than it has any right to. Six miles on the river path, the cold kind where your face hurts and you feel righteous about it. Came home and worked on the story for two hours. The keeper has a daughter now. I wasn't planning that. She showed up.

Coffee with Sam, who I haven't seen since the wedding two years ago. He's a recruiter at a smaller firm in Fort Point. He didn't push. He just listened and then said 'we'd be lucky to talk to you' in a way that didn't feel like a line. I walked back along the Greenway and the wind off the harbor was sharp and somehow I was smiling.

Saw Maya at the Trader Joe's on Memorial Drive. We both froze in the cheese aisle. She looked good. I think I did too, or at least not bad. We hugged. Short. Real. I bought the wrong yogurt because I couldn't think straight after and I didn't realize until I got home.

Finished a real draft of the lighthouse story. 4,300 words. Sent it to Priya with a long apologetic email and then deleted the apologetic parts and sent it again. The keeper finds his glasses on his head at the end. It's not a clever ending. I think I like it anyway.

Second interview with Sam's company on Thursday. Pulled out the navy sweater Maya bought me two birthdays ago because it still looks good and I refuse to be sentimental about a sweater. Tom from board game night texted to ask if I wanted to do a Sunday running thing with him and his roommate. Said yes.

Shortest day of the year. Made the bolognese again. Ate it on the couch with the lights off except for the string ones. Read for two hours straight, which I haven't done in I don't know how long. Hannah Sullivan poems. The line about the snow coming on. Snow did come on, actually. Light, the kind that doesn't stick.

Got the offer. 18% more than I make now. They want me to start Feb 3. Drove down to my parents' for the day after Christmas and told them in the kitchen while Mom was scrubbing a roasting pan. She hugged me for too long. Dad just nodded the slow Dad nod and said 'good, kid.' I didn't realize until tonight that the rent panic has been gone for three days and I didn't notice it leave.

Spent New Year's Eve at Tom's. Twelve people, the dog Mochi in a little party hat, someone made an extremely complicated cocktail involving rosemary. Came home before 1. Stood on the fire escape in my coat looking at the bricks across the alley. I am not going to pretend this was a good year. I am also not going to pretend I am the same person who started it.

Put in my notice. Devin took it better than I expected. Or worse, depending on how you read it. He said 'I always thought you'd be here longer' and went back to his laptop. Walked to the river at lunch. The Charles was half frozen. A guy was throwing a tennis ball for a yellow lab and the ball kept skidding across the ice and the dog kept going after it with this beautiful confused joy.

Priya sent back the story with notes in a Google Doc, the kind with the long comments and the short ones, the short ones being the brutal ones. She wants me to cut the daughter scene. I knew she would. I am going to fight her on it for a week and then probably cut it. Made coffee at the window. The guy across the courtyard was watering his plants again, in a different robe this time. Comforting in a way I can't explain.

Ran seven miles, my longest since summer. Came back, stretched on the kitchen floor, listened to the radiator do its thing. Saw a text from Maya wishing me luck on the new job and I sat with it for a while before I answered. I answered kindly. Then I closed the phone and went and worked on the story. The keeper still loses his glasses. I haven't figured out where the daughter goes yet. I don't have to figure it out today.
